Prevention: Alloshe, Numan, Ashebeka, Tumsa, Dosha, Obse, Gebelcho or
Plant seeds free from chocolate spot disease.
Practice crop rotation every 2-3 years with non-host crops (Wheat, Barley, Maize).
Do not sow disease free seeds in previously chocolate spot pathogen infected field, use disease free seeds in disease free field or keep a distance of at least 500m from infected fields.
Avoid high planting density this will reduce the humidity which triggers the aggressive phase of the disease.
Check correct spacing for each variety.
Remove crop debris and volunteer bean plants like chickpea, lentils, vetch beans etc) and destroy by burning.
Make sure adequate drainage is provided and use correct rate of fertilizer.
Minimize movement from infected to disease free fields.
Deep plowing of the fields with high chocolate spot infection immediately after harvest reduces the risk of disease development.
Rhizobium (10 g/kg faba bean seeds) before sowing improve plant health and indirectily reduce chocolate spot severity.
Monitoring: Start monitoring the crop from emergence of leaves until maturity as there are 2 phases to the disease.
Non- aggressive phase: look for small brown/red spots peppered over the leaves also on stems, pods and flowers.
During high humidity the aggressive phase develops: grey fungus grows on the spots as they become larger and darker, defoliation can follow.
Young pods and flower can abort or become stunted.
Brown streaks appear on stems and can cause them to lodge.

Consider applying a protectant fungicide when plants show the first symptoms of the disease espcially if the weather is forcasted to be wet - taking action when there are 5-10 spots per leaf or 3-5 leaves per plant infected.
Sowing date with a resistant (tolerant) variety and judicious use of fungicide can be used as good option of chocolate spot management.
Direct Control: Remove severely affected plants and destroy by burying or burning to reduce the source of inoculum on the farm
Restrictions: When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label.
Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance.
